per_token.statistic: median over 20 tokens (sorted value at index n/2), each field's median taken on its own, so derived differences are differences of medians

graph.sems_done_note: not written by gpu_decode_graph_test; submit_now() in omega_gpu_decode_graph.c fails the token when sems_done != launches, so a PASS run implies sems_done == launches for every timed token (inferred, not a recorded value)

flush_each.sems_done_note: as for graph: not recorded, implied by the PASS verdict
flush_each.note: the same recorded list submitted one launch per submission (TEST ONLY set_flush_each): the batching comparison inside the same run

stamped_token.note: one extra token run with set_stamps(1): span_ns and stage times are device PTIMER differences; chip_ns is that token's host-clock submit span; unattributed_ns = chip_ns - span_ns (submit call, front-end start, completion marker and host poll)

aggregate.reason: the input receipt carries per-token medians and one stamped token only, no per-token arrays or run totals, so no aggregate sums or percentiles are derived (adding them needs the test to write every token's stats)

serial_vs_overlap.chip_ns: serial: the sum over the token's submissions of one host-clock span each (1 submission per graph token, 22 per flush_each token); spans never overlap each other
serial_vs_overlap.stages: serial partition: barrier 0 (wfi+inval_all) puts a WAIT_FOR_IDLE before every stamp and prefetch is off, so launches run one after another and the stage times add up exactly to span_ns
serial_vs_overlap.reason: every launch waits for the previous one (WFI) and the host records before it submits, so nothing overlaps to measure; device time inside the host span is span_ns, the rest is unattributed_ns

methodology.device_clock: GPU PTIMER ns from compute-class REPORT_SEMAPHORE timestamps (omega_gpu_cmdlist.h: "out[0] = GPU timestamp (ns, PTIMER) before launch 0, out[i + 1] = after launch i completed (taken after its WAIT_FOR_IDLE)"); used only by stamped_token span_ns and stages
methodology.host_clock: omega_gpu_session_now_ns(): the platform's time_now_ns, CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Linux (omega_gpu_platform_linux.c ref_now_ns); used by chip_ns, record_ns and total_ns

counters.chip_ns: omega_gpu_decode_graph.h: "sum of the list submissions' first-submit-to-last-marker time". HOST clock, not device time: omega_gpu_cmdlist_submit() reads time_now_ns just before queue_submit and again after both completion marker words were seen and synced, so it holds device execution plus submit, fetch and poll latency
counters.stamps: omega_gpu_decode_graph.h: "Launch i took stamps[i + 1] - stamps[i] ns"; gpu_decode_graph_test sums them per kind (per_kind_ns)
counters.host_overhead_ns: derived: total_ns - chip_ns, both host clock: recording, attention counter check, output sync, token read and lock, everything outside the submit span

methodology.source: numbers copied from the stats file written by tests/gpu_decode_graph_test.c --out; settings from its log; identity from the runner's device.txt and binaries.sha256

limitations: chip_ns is host-clock time around the device work; the only device-clock numbers are the stamped token's span_ns and stages

per-token values are independent medians of a synthetic step on random weights (Qwen3-30B-A3B shapes, not a checkpoint), one fixed position, the same token every rep; not a serving or end-to-end tokens-per-second figure
the stamped token is a single token: its stage times are one sample, not a distribution
sems_done, the command list's own host_ns (method-stream build) and the marker-wait part of chip_ns are not recorded per token
no aggregate totals or percentiles: the input has medians only
